data.long_meaning: Derived from the Slavic name Kazimierz, meaning 'full of sorrow'. In Christian tradition, the name is associated with St. Casimir, a Polish prince and patron saint of Lithuania. He is known for his deep faith, purity, and dedication to God. The name Kasimir carries the meaning “Full of sorrow, purity” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Kasimir usually hope their child will grow to embody full of sorrow, purity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
